The following notes are based on a set of five lectures given by R. Serber during the first two weeks of April 1943, as an "indoctrination course" in connection with the starting of the Los Alamos Project. The notes were written up by E. U. Condon.

The object of the project is to produce a practical military weapon in the form of a bomb in which the energy is released by a fast neutron chain reaction in one or more of the materials known to show nuclear fission.

plain: The physicist Edward Condon, Michels says, went from the inner circle of the atomic bomb project to leading the study that shut down serious UFO research. Michels tells it himself, linking Condon to Oppenheimer, to the physicist Max Born in Göttingen, Germany, where Condon studied in the 1920s, and to General Leslie Groves, who ran the bomb project. In his telling Condon's security clearance was lost, then "randomly he pops back up in 1966 and his clearance is mysteriously restored", and he is placed on a panel "which deals a death blow to UFO research claiming it's all a waste of time and money." The record he points to is the Los Alamos Primer, the April 1943 notes from the first lectures of the bomb project. It says the notes are "based on a set of five lectures given by R. Serber", the physicist Robert Serber, as an "indoctrination course" at the start of the Los Alamos Project, and that "the notes were written up by E. U. Condon." It states the goal: "to produce a practical military weapon in the form of a bomb." That puts Condon at the very start of the bomb work, as Michels says. Being from 1943, it cannot speak to his later clearance or his UFO study. If Michels is right, the man who closed the book on UFOs was a trusted atomic insider.

discussion.text: The Primer places Condon at the start of the Los Alamos Project in April 1943, writing up Serber's lectures on the bomb; being from 1943 it cannot speak to his later clearance or his UFO study.
